name: Riga International Airport
before:
The largest airport in the Baltic states, about 10 km west of Riga, with direct flights to 107 destinations as of September 2024. It is the hub for airBaltic and a base for Ryanair and Norwegian.

The pier layout is worth knowing. There is one two storey terminal with 36 check in counters in a single row. Airside, the B pier handles Schengen flights and the C pier takes both Schengen and non-Schengen, with eight jetbridge stands between them plus walk-boarding and bus gates. The original boarding area A is now used only for some arrivals.

Ground transport is simpler than it was. Bus line 22 runs between the city centre and the airport. A shuttle from the international bus terminal was tried in 2024 but dropped in 2025 for lack of demand, so the city bus is the option.

The single runway is 3,200 metres with a Category II instrument approach.

A master plan adds a south pier and a new control tower. Both airBaltic and the Latvian Civil Aviation Agency have their head offices here.
after:
The largest airport in the Baltic states, about 10 km west of Riga. Latvia's national airline, airBaltic, flies from here. Ryanair also has a base.

Bus 22 runs between the city centre and the airport.

Its single runway is 3,200 metres long. The Latvian Civil Aviation Agency has its head office at the airport.
